newsitem.title: USA: Telephone and Data Q2 hurt by Aerial start-up.
newsitem.headline: Telephone and Data Q2 hurt by Aerial start-up.

text.p: Telephone and Data Systems Inc said Wednesday its second-quarter earnings were hurt by costs associated with starting operations in Aerial Communications Inc's personal communication services (PCS) markets.
Aerial, which is 82.6 percent owned by Telephone and Data, reported a second-quarter loss of $55.5 million or $0.78 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $7.2 million or $0.11.
Aerial, which operated only in Columbus, Ohio, at the start of the second quarter, has since rolled out service in Houston, Minneapolis, Kansas City, Pittsburgh and Tampa.

U.S. Cellular Corp, Telephone and Data's 80.9 percent-owned subsidiary, saw a 28.4 percent rise in operating revenues to $217.6 million. Operating income before gains rose to $0.33 a share from $0.23.
American Paging Inc, its 82 percent-owned subsidiary, had a loss of $0.56 a share compared with a year-ago loss of $0.42.

Second-quarter operating cash flow for American Paging was a positive $312,000 for the second quarter, compared with a negative $707,000 in the first quarter. But it declined from a positive $927,000 in the year-ago second quarter.
